question: The Sannyasi-Fakir Rebellion commenced in the second half of which of the following centuries?
solution:
The correct answer is __**18th Century**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Sannyasi-Fakir Rebellion took place during the **second half of the 18th century** (1760s to 1800).
 
• This rebellion was primarily led by Hindu **Sannyasis** (ascetics) and Muslim **Fakirs** (mendicants) against the oppressive policies of the British East India Company.
 
• The rebellion was caused by excessive **taxation policies, exploitation, and restrictions** imposed by the British on religious mendicants who traditionally moved freely across the Bengal region.
 
• The region most impacted by the rebellion included **Bengal and Bihar**, which were under the British East India Company's control during this period.
 
• Key leaders of the movement included **Majnu Shah** and other Fakir and Sannyasi leaders, who mobilized local peasants, tribals, and other marginalized communities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sannyasi-Fakir Rebellion**

 
 
• The rebellion is often considered one of the earliest forms of resistance against British colonial rule in India.
 
• It set a precedent for future uprisings and revolts against the East India Company's exploitative policies.
 
• The cultural and religious unity displayed by Hindus and Muslims during the rebellion is a significant aspect of this historical event.
